The disposable underpants-type diaper includes outer members having stretchable regions positioned adjacent to the inner edges of the side seal portions. Each stretchable region includes a plurality of elongated elastic members arranged at predetermined intervals in the front-back direction and extending in the width direction. The elastic members are disposed between two sheet layers, with both ends of each elastic member fixed to the layers. By contrast, the intermediate portion of each elastic member between its fixed ends remains unattached to either sheet layer, allowing the elastic member to stretch and contract freely.

The two sheet layers are welded together in the spaces between adjacent elastic members. The resulting bonding sections are confined within the stretchable regions and do not protrude outward from the side seal portions. This arrangement maintains the elasticity of the regions while providing secure integration of the sheet layers and a smooth configuration around the side seals.
outputs.L4:
An underpants-type disposable diaper includes a front body portion, a rear body portion, and a crotch portion extending between them. Opposing side edge regions of the front and rear body portions are joined by side seals to form a waist opening and a pair of leg openings. At least one of the body portions includes a stretchable region formed by first and second sheet layers and a plurality of elastic members disposed between the sheet layers. The elastic members extend in the diaper’s width direction near the side seals.

Each elastic member has end portions fixed to the sheet layers and an intermediate portion that is not fixed, or is fixed less strongly, so that the elastic member can contract and stretch effectively. Bonding sections joining the first and second sheet layers are arranged between adjacent elastic members. These bonding sections stabilize the layered structure and help maintain the intended spacing and position of the elastic members without unnecessarily restricting their elasticity.

In the stretchable regions adjacent to the side seals, the bonding sections are configured so that they do not protrude outward from the side seals. Accordingly, no bonded projection or hardened laminate portion extends beyond the sealed side edges. This arrangement produces a cleaner and smoother edge, reduces unnecessary thickness and stiffness near the wearer’s sides, and improves the appearance and feel of the diaper. At the same time, the unfixed intermediate sections of the elastic members retain sufficient freedom to expand and contract, thereby preserving a comfortable fit and reliable elasticity around the wearer’s waist and body.
outputs.L5:
### The Power of “The”

“The” is one of the smallest yet most important words in the English language. Known as the definite article, it points to a specific person, place, object, or idea. When we say “the book,” we usually mean a particular book that the listener already knows about or can identify.

Although “the” may seem insignificant, it adds clarity and precision to communication. Compare “I saw a dog” with “I saw the dog.” The first sentence refers to any dog, while the second suggests a specific one.

The word also appears in countless titles, expressions, and names, from *The Great Gatsby* to “the beginning of the end.” Its simplicity makes it almost invisible, but language would feel far less natural without it. In just three letters, “the” helps turn general thoughts into specific meaning.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a concise patent-style description of a disposable pull-on diaper with stretchable regions near the side seals, elastic members between two sheet layers, and bonding sections that do not protrude from the side seal portions.
counterfactuals.output: A disposable pull-on diaper comprises an absorbent body, a front waist region, a rear waist region, and a crotch region extending therebetween. Opposed side portions of the front and rear waist regions are joined at side seal portions to define a waist opening and a pair of leg openings. Each waist region includes first and second sheet layers and stretchable regions adjacent to the side seal portions. A plurality of elastic members is disposed between the first and second sheet layers and secured thereto by bonding sections. counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Explain how the outer members 12F and 12B, elastically stretchable members 19, sheet layers 12S and 12H, and sheet bonding sections 20 are arranged in the disclosed diaper.
counterfactuals.output:
- **Outer members 12F and 12B** form the exterior of the diaper’s front and back waist regions, respectively. They are separate across the crotch and are joined together at their lateral edges to form the waist opening and leg openings.

- Each outer member is made from two superposed sheet layers: an **outer sheet layer 12S** and an **inner sheet layer 12H**.

- A plurality of elongated, **elastically stretchable members 19** are disposed between sheet layers 12S and 12H, generally extending in the diaper’s lateral or waist-circumference direction. When relaxed, they contract the outer members and create gathers; when worn, they stretch to provide a close fit.

- **Sheet bonding sections 20** bond sheet layers 12S and 12H together at spaced locations. The bonding sections are arranged intermittently, with the elastic members 19 running through or between them. Thus, the sheets are not bonded over their entire surfaces: the unbonded portions can bulge or fold as the elastic members contract, while the bonding sections maintain the laminated structure and control the resulting gathers.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe an underpants-type disposable diaper in which widthwise elastic members have fixed ends and unfixed intermediate sections, with welded sheet bonding sections positioned between adjacent elastic members.
counterfactuals.output:
An underpants-type disposable diaper includes a front waist region, a rear waist region, and a crotch region, with the lateral edges of the front and rear waist regions joined to form a waist opening and two leg openings. An absorbent body is disposed on the skin-facing side of an outer sheet assembly.

A plurality of elastic members extend in the diaper width direction within at least one waist region and are spaced apart in the longitudinal direction. Each elastic member has opposite end portions fixed to the surrounding sheets, while an intermediate section between the fixed end portions remains unfixed to the sheets, allowing the elastic to contract freely.

The sheets are joined by discrete welded bonding sections located between adjacent elastic members in the longitudinal direction. The welded sections bond the sheets without directly fixing or crossing the unfixed intermediate sections of the elastic members. This arrangement maintains sheet integrity and controls gathering while permitting independent contraction of the elastic members, thereby improving waist fit, flexibility, and comfort.
